name: David Citadel Hotel
positioning: Luxury hotel designed by Piero Lissoni, within walking distance of Jerusalem's Old City and the city center
best_for: Travelers who want to walk to the Old City and the city center
Families who need a room for two adults and two children

facts.text: The hotel is within walking distance of the Old City and the city center.
The Royal Suite was designed for visiting dignitaries and international heads of state.
The Royal Suite has a kitchenette with its own separate entrance for hotel servers.
Rooms come with Frette linen and Bvlgari amenities.
The Citadel Old City View Suite has two bathrooms, each with a bathtub, a separate shower and Carrara marble tiles.
The Premium Executive Suite has oak parquet flooring and sketches of ancient Jerusalem.
The Deluxe room with pool view has a furnished balcony with partial views of the Old City and the pool.
The Superior Family Room sleeps two adults and two children, or three adults.
The hotel has one of the most spacious gyms in Jerusalem.
The hotel's team has been curating tailored events for over two decades.

highlights.text: The Royal Suite is named in honor of former Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin.
The hotel's location connects the Old City with the new, so guests can stroll to famous sites.
Rooms and suites are designed by Italian designer Piero Lissoni.
The Royal Suite has a spacious balcony with views of the Old City of Jerusalem.
The Veranda Fine Grill Restaurant has a view of the Old City Walls.

considerations.text: The hotel is kosher, under the supervision of the Jerusalem Rabbinate.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
WhataHotel notes the hotel is in a busy tourist area that can be crowded.
